subtopic: Found money or a lost wallet
subtype: Approach: handing it to a responsible adult [Action]
passage: When I was eleven, I, Lakshmi, found a wallet on the bus to school. Nobody was near. I could have put it in my bag and no one would ever know. Instead I walked to the conductor and handed it over. "There are cards inside," I told him. "They will show the owner's name." Then at school I went to Binita Miss and told her what I had done. Why both? I thought, if two grown-ups know, nobody can ever say Lakshmi took a single rupee. Binita Miss wrote it in the school diary and smiled. Two days later the owner came to thank the conductor, and I was proud in a quiet way.

qa.q: Who did Lakshmi give the wallet to on the bus?
qa.a: Lakshmi gave it to the conductor.

qa.q: What was Lakshmi worried about when she thought of telling two grown-ups?
qa.a: She wanted to be sure nobody could say she took anything, so she felt careful and wanted to be clear.

qa.q: What choice inside the story made the plan work?
qa.a: She handed the wallet to the conductor and also told her teacher, so the cards could trace the owner and she was covered.

qa.q: How did Binita Miss see what Lakshmi had done?
qa.a: Binita Miss took it as a responsible act, writing it in the school diary and smiling.

grounding: A girl gives a found wallet to the conductor and tells her teacher, so the cards can lead to the owner.

subtopic: Found money or a lost wallet
subtype: Approach: handing it to a responsible adult [Action]
passage: The bus was jammed, it was raining, and Yamini had only two stops to go when she spotted a leather wallet on the floor by her feet. People were pushing. There was no time to look inside, and she didn't want to. She squeezed to the front and held it up to the conductor. "Bhaiya, this was on the floor near the back." He wrote down the time and route. At school she went straight to her teacher, Sharmila ma'am, and told her what had happened, and which bus it was. "The conductor has it. There might be an ID card inside." Sharmila ma'am called the bus depot during lunch. The owner's card was inside, and by evening he had it back.

qa.q: What did the conductor write down?
How did Yamini feel about looking inside the wallet?
qa.a: She didn't want to, perhaps feeling that handing it on untouched was more honest and safer.

qa.q: What else could Yamini do if there had been no conductor?
qa.a: She could give it to a teacher or the school office, so a responsible adult can trace the owner.

qa.q: How does Yamini's report look to Sharmila ma'am?
qa.a: Sharmila ma'am trusts it and follows up with the depot, pleased that Yamini told her straight away.

grounding: It shows a girl handing a found wallet to the conductor and telling her teacher, so the owner can be traced and nobody can say she took anything.

subtopic: Found money or a lost wallet
subtype: Approach: handing it to a responsible adult [Action]
passage: Walking to school in Ludhiana, Gurpreet found a wallet lying near the bus stop. She picked it up carefully. She didn't open it. A shopkeeper nearby watched her. "Keep it, who'll know?" he joked. Gurpreet shook her head. She walked straight to the traffic police booth on the corner and gave it to the officer there, saying exactly where she'd found it. Then at school she told her class teacher, Reena ma'am, including the booth and the time. "Good," said Reena ma'am. "Now two adults know, and nobody can say anything went missing." The officer found an ID card inside and called the owner. By lunch, the man had it back.

qa.q: Where did Gurpreet take the wallet?
qa.a: To the traffic police booth on the corner.

qa.q: How did Gurpreet feel when the shopkeeper joked about keeping it?
qa.a: She seemed calm and sure, shaking her head because she had already decided to hand it in.

qa.q: What else could Gurpreet do if the booth had been empty?
qa.a: She could take it straight to school and give it to Reena ma'am, who could contact the police or owner.

qa.q: How does the handover look to Reena ma'am?
qa.a: Reena ma'am is pleased, seeing that telling two adults protects both the owner and Gurpreet.

grounding: It shows a girl handing a found wallet to a responsible adult and telling her teacher, so the owner can be traced and nobody can say she took anything.
